newsitem.title: USA: White House unconcerned by latest U.S. indicators.
newsitem.headline: White House unconcerned by latest U.S. indicators.

text.p: The White House said on Monday it was not concerned about new economic indicators showing consumer spending was slowing and spending on new construction dropping.

"The fact that the economy would slow a little bit is not seen as a negative here given the very strong performance that we talked about in the first quarter," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters.
Spending on all types of new construction dropped in April for the first time in four months, the Commerce Department said Monday, though the housing sector remained exceptionally strong.
Total spending dropped one percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of $596.9 billion after a sharply revised 0.1 percent increase in March that previously was reported as a 0.2 percent decrase.
The falloff in April construction spending was the first since last December, when it also was down by 1 percent.
Consumer spending edged up at its slowest rate in seven months during April, the Department also said, kept in check by slim income gains in a fresh sign of slowing economic momentum.

Spending rose just 0.1 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of $5.35 trillion after a revised 0.2 percent increase in March. Incomes from wages, salaries and all other sources were up an identical 0.1 percent to a rate of $6.75 trillion following a strong 0.6 percent rise in March.
